documents.title: BeatKana

metadata.description: An educational rhythm game built in Unity that teaches Japanese Hiragana through timing-based gameplay.

documents.text:
### BeatKana

##### Overview

An educational rhythm game built in Unity that teaches Japanese Hiragana through timing-based gameplay. Unlike flashcard-style educational games, BeatKana reinforces real reading fluency — kana recognition speed, sound recall, and typing accuracy under timing pressure.

##### Core Features

Rhythm-based gameplay — players input Hiragana on beat-based timelines including dakuten, palatalized combinations, and combo-note structures

Custom kana keyboard — built specifically for gameplay with progression-based key unlocking, avoiding mobile input friction and latency issues

Data-driven progression — structured around language acquisition concepts with accuracy-based unlocks, mastery systems, and procedural endless modes

##### Architecture

A major emphasis of the project was building reusable, scalable systems rather than hardcoded level logic. Gameplay is driven through a custom timeline and queue architecture that dynamically generates note structures and manages input timing windows, combo progression, and failure recovery via state machines.

Content is authored through Unity Scriptable Objects covering kana metadata, pitch-accent information, progression data, and sound behavior — allowing the game to scale without rewriting gameplay systems. Pitch-accent data was processed through a custom pipeline that parsed public linguistic data and exported it directly into Unity assets.

##### Planned

Android and iOS deployment, Katakana support, Kanji-assisted modes, adaptive difficulty, and expanded procedural content generation.

documents.text:
### Learn To Drive

Play In-Browser Demo

##### Overview

A 2D top-down mobile game designed to teach children the real mechanics of driving. Players interact with an on-screen dashboard — gas, brake, steering wheel, and other car functions — to navigate driving scenarios safely and build foundational road awareness.

##### Core Features

Realistic controls — interactive dashboard with gas, brake, steering wheel, and other car functions mapped to touch input

Top-down driving — 2D above-view perspective built for mobile with an open world to explore

Educational focus — designed for children to learn safe driving habits and understand how a car operates before ever sitting behind a real wheel

documents.title: F1ForHelp API

metadata.description: A self-hosted Python FastAPI backend for f1forhelp.dev with an AI Q&A built on Claude, plus the contact form and visit counter. A full rebuild of an earlier Laravel API.

documents.text:
##### Overview

A self-hosted Python API that powers the backend of f1forhelp.dev. It handles the contact form, the visit counter, and an AI Q&A that answers visitor questions about Nick using this site's own content. It runs in Docker on a personal Linux server and is reached through a Cloudflare Tunnel at api.f1forhelp.dev.

This is version 2: a full rebuild of the original Laravel API (see Version History below), redesigned around self-hosting and AI features.

##### Try It: AI Q&A

Ask a question about Nick, his projects, or this site. The answer is generated live by the API from the site's content.

##### How the AI Q&A Works

The site is the knowledge source — when the site is deployed, a build step converts the project pages to plain text and publishes them as knowledge.json. The API loads that file on startup and on demand, keeps a cached copy, and rejects a broken publish instead of replacing a good one.

Structured output — Claude (Haiku 5.5) returns the answer, whether the question was in scope, which pages it used, and topic tags, all validated against a schema. Source links are checked against the real pages, so the model can't link to a page that doesn't exist.

Grounded, third-person answers — the model answers only from the site's content, refers to Nick in the third person, says when the site doesn't cover something, and declines off-topic requests.

Prompt injection defenses — visitor text is wrapped and escaped so it can't break out of its section of the prompt, and the model is told to treat it as data. The model has no tools, and its output is only displayed as plain text.

Cost and abuse controls — per-visitor limits per minute and per day, a site-wide daily cap, prompt caching, and token usage and estimated cost logged for every request.

Feedback loop — every question is logged, visitors can rate answers, and questions the content couldn't answer are reported so the site can be improved.

Contact triage — new contact messages are classified by category and urgency with a one-line summary, which is included in the notification Nick receives.

##### Endpoints

POST /ask — answers one question from the site's content. Returns the answer, an in-scope flag, and source links

POST /ask/{id}/feedback — marks an answer helpful or not; only the visitor who asked can rate it, once

GET /knowledge — which build of the site's content the Q&A is using

POST /contact — accepts name, email, and message. Returns 201 on success, 422 on validation failure, 429 on rate limit

GET /counter and POST /counter/increment — the visit counter

GET /health — server status, including whether the AI features are ready

Admin endpoints — status reports and content refresh, protected by a key and rate limited

Interactive API docs: api.f1forhelp.dev/docs

##### Security

No open ports — the server only makes an outbound connection to Cloudflare, which handles HTTPS. Nothing on the server listens on the public internet

Rate limiting — per visitor IP, read from Cloudflare's connecting-IP header since every request arrives through the tunnel

IP hashing — SHA-256 with a salt, never stored raw and never returned in responses

Honeypot field — bot submissions get a normal-looking response but are never stored

Safe queries and locked-down CORS — parameterized SQL throughout, and only this site's origins can call the API from a browser

##### Architecture & Hosting

Request path — browser → Cloudflare (HTTPS) → Cloudflare Tunnel → FastAPI container, which talks to SQLite, the Claude API, and a Discord webhook for notifications

Docker Compose — the API and the tunnel run as two containers on a personal Linux server; deploying is a git pull and a rebuild

SQLite with versioned migrations — the database lives in a Docker volume that survives rebuilds, and schema changes apply automatically on startup

Organized for growth — endpoints, shared infrastructure, and business logic are kept in separate layers, with configuration from environment variables and an automated test suite that mocks the Claude API

##### Live Demo: Counter

This counter is backed by the live API. Hit the button and the counter persists across sessions and visitors.

Increment

##### Version History

###### v1 — Laravel on Railway

The first version of this backend was a Laravel (PHP) REST API deployed on Railway. It handled contact form submissions and exposed the visit counter, with a public Railway URL.

Endpoints — POST /api/contact (201 / 422 / 429), GET /api/counter, POST /api/counter/increment

Security — 5 requests per minute per IP via Laravel's throttle middleware, a honeypot field, salted SHA-256 IP hashing, and Eloquent ORM for SQL injection protection

Hosting — Railway, at f1forhelp-api-production.up.railway.app

Source: github.com/nick-ulmer/f1forhelp-api

###### v2 — The Rebuild

Why — to self-host the backend, move to Python for AI work, and add AI features to the site

Kept — the contact and counter behavior, response codes, validation error format, and security measures, so the frontend only needed its API address and paths updated

Changed — Laravel/PHP → Python/FastAPI, Railway → self-hosted Docker behind a Cloudflare Tunnel, the /api prefix dropped from routes, and a layered project structure with automatic database migrations and tests

Added — the AI Q&A built on the site's own content, AI triage of contact messages, Discord notifications and status reports, and usage and cost logging

documents.title: F1ForHelp.dev

metadata.description: A personal portfolio site built with React, Vite, and MDX.

documents.text:
### F1ForHelp.dev

##### Overview

This site. A personal portfolio built from scratch with React and Vite, designed to showcase projects across software, game development, and data science. Each project page is authored in MDX, making it easy to mix structured data with rich content without maintaining a backend or CMS. Built with a lot of iteration and assistance from Claude AI.

##### Stack & Architecture

React + Vite — fast dev experience with a clean build pipeline and path alias support via @/ imports

MDX project pages — each project is a self-contained MDX file exporting its own metadata object, making the content and the config live in one place

Material UI — MUI v9 with Emotion for consistent design tokens, layout, and component styling across the site

##### Status

Actively developed alongside the projects it documents. New project pages and features are added on an ongoing basis.

documents.title: Trip Data & Analytics

metadata.description: Automated R script that extracts screenshot text and compiles IRS-compliant mileage logs for delivery drivers.

documents.text:
### Trip Data & Analytics

##### Overview

An automated R pipeline built for Spark Driver gig workers. Rather than manually logging every delivery trip, drivers simply take screenshots of the Spark app during their shifts. The script handles everything else — reading the images, extracting trip data, calculating mileage via Google Maps, and producing a clean IRS-compliant log ready for tax filing.

##### How It Works

OCR ingestion — scans a folder of Spark Driver screenshots, parses dates from filenames, and extracts raw trip text using optical character recognition

Trip leg construction — regex identifies store origins and delivery addresses, splits multi-stop trips into individual pickup and drop-off legs, and queries the Google Maps Distance API for accurate driving mileage

IRS log generation — applies the standard IRS mileage rate, calculates deductible value per leg, and exports a structured CSV with from/to addresses, purpose, miles, duration, and dollar value

##### Status

Complete. Built and used for the 2024 tax year. Potential future work includes a UI wrapper or automated screenshot import from mobile.
